note: Bodies the Province consolidates in its Public Accounts (the government reporting entity) that the atlas did not have, added 2026-11-27 from research/finance/public-accounts-23-1/missing.csv. Each was re-checked against its own financial statements, the statute that set it up or ended it, and BC Registries (OrgBook BC) for societies and companies. A date is given only where a source gives it; otherwise the start is a sighting (firstSeen) or the end is untraced. Responsible ministries are given only where a source assigns one (Creston Valley); the employers’ associations answer to the Public Sector Employers’ Council, not a ministry, and are left without one. Discovery Enterprises Inc. and BCIF Management Ltd. were recommended as related bodies; their statements show both were wholly owned by the Province, so they are atlas bodies here.

records.name: British Columbia Public School Employers' Association
records.description: The employers’ association for the K–12 public school sector under the Public Sector Employers Act, which requires an association for each public sector other than the public service. It coordinates compensation, benefits, human resource practices and bargaining for the boards of education, and is the accredited bargaining agent for school boards. A society controlled by the Province and consolidated in its accounts since 2010-11; its year ends on 30 June.
records.establishedMeaning: registered as a society; BCPSEA’s own history says it was formed in May 1994, under the Public Sector Employers Act of 1993
records.establishedLocator: BC Registries (OrgBook BC), society S0032506, registration 12 September 1994

records.name: Community Social Services Employers' Association of British Columbia
records.description: The employers’ association for the community social services sector under the Public Sector Employers Act. It provides human resources and labour relations services to more than 200 member social service organizations. Consolidated in the Province’s accounts since 2010-11.
records.establishedMeaning: constituted and registered as a society
records.establishedLocator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1, Operations: “constituted on January 13, 1994 and is incorporated under the Societies Act”; BC Registries society S0031460 gives the same day

records.name: Health Employers Association of British Columbia
records.description: The employers’ association for the health sector under the Public Sector Employers Act. It coordinates collective bargaining and exempt compensation and supports health employers with benefits administration and human resource practice. Consolidated in the Province’s accounts since 2010-11.
records.establishedMeaning: formed by the amalgamation of the Continuing Care Employee Relations Association, the Health Labour Relations Association and the labour relations division of the B.C. Association of Private Care, following the Korbin Commission
records.establishedLocator: HEABC Annual Report 1994–95, “On December 1, 1993, HEABC became that singular employer organization through the amalgamation of…”; BC Registries society S0031292 records an amalgamation on the same day

records.name: Post-Secondary Employers' Association
records.description: The employers’ association for public colleges, institutes and special-purpose teaching universities under the Public Sector Employers Act. It bargains collectively for its 19 member institutions and advises them on labour relations and human resources. Consolidated in the Province’s accounts since 2010-11.
records.establishedMeaning: registered as a society (“The Post-Secondary Employers’ Association”) under the authority of the Public Sector Employers Act
records.establishedLocator: BC Registries (OrgBook BC), society S0031981, registration 17 May 1994

records.name: Crown Corporations Employers Association
records.description: The employers’ association for Crown corporations, agencies and commissions under the Public Sector Employers Act; its statements describe it as a Crown corporation that follows the strategic direction of the Public Sector Employers’ Council. Consolidated in the Province’s accounts since 2011-12.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated as a society
records.establishedLocator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1: “was incorporated on 11 February 1994”; BC Registries society S0031583 gives the same day

records.name: Organized Crime Agency of British Columbia
records.description: A society and designated policing unit created on the Owen Report’s recommendation to replace the Coordinated Law Enforcement Unit. Since 2004 its sworn and civilian members serve within the Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of B.C. (CFSEU-BC). The Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General appoints its directors.
records.establishedMeaning: established as a Designated Policing and Law Enforcement Unit under the Police Act; the society was registered on 15 March 1999
records.establishedLocator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1, Nature of operations: “established as a Designated Policing and Law Enforcement Unit on March 23, 1999, under the Police Act”

records.name: Creston Valley Wildlife Management Authority

responsible.ministry: Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship
responsible.locator: OIC 568/2023: the Creston Valley Wildlife Act assigned to the Minister of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship
responsible.note: The minister responsible for the Act, under which the authority answers (s. 22). Earlier assignments of the Act are listed in the atlas’s Acts and ministerial responsibility record.

records.description: The statutory authority that manages the Creston Valley Wildlife Management Area, about 7,000 hectares of provincial Crown land on the Kootenay River held in trust for wildlife conservation. Its members are a provincial official, the director of the Canadian Wildlife Service and others under section 16 of the Act. Its trust fund has been consolidated in the Province’s accounts every year since 1999-2000.
records.establishedMeaning: the Creston Valley Wildlife Act, passed in March 1968, set up the management area and its management authority; the Act’s commencement day is not given here
records.establishedLocator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1(a): the Trust Fund “was established in 1968 by the Creston Valley Wildlife Act”, administered by the Management Authority

records.name: British Columbia Racing Commission
records.description: The horse-racing regulator, continued as a corporation of one or more members appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council under the Horse Racing Act. The Public Accounts consolidated its Horse Racing Improvement Fund, which the Ministry of Public Safety and Solicitor General administered; the fund ceased operations on 31 March 2003 under the Gaming Control Act. When the commission was first established is not established here.

firstSeen.locator: Public Accounts 2001-02, financial statements of the British Columbia Racing Commission Horse Racing Improvement Fund, year ended 31 March 2002

records.endedMeaning: the Horse Racing Act, which continued the commission as a corporation, was repealed by the Gaming Control Act (2002-14-110), effective 1 April 2003 (B.C. Reg. 59/2003)

records.name: Okanagan Valley Tree Fruit Authority
records.description: A statutory authority set up to revitalize the tree fruit industry in the B.C. Interior, chiefly through orchard replanting programs. On 12 March 2003 the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Fisheries entered a trust agreement with the B.C. Investment Agriculture Foundation to continue those programs, and the authority’s remaining funds went to the foundation and the ministry.
records.establishedMeaning: the Okanagan Valley Tree Fruit Authority Act came into force
records.endedMeaning: the Act was repealed by order of the Lieutenant Governor in Council made on 6 March 2003, effective 31 May 2003; its orchard renovation programs continued under a trust agreement with the B.C. Investment Agriculture Foundation

records.name: Forensic Psychiatric Services Commission
records.description: Runs the Forensic Psychiatric Hospital and community forensic clinics, assesses fitness for the courts and treats people found not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder. From 2001 it was a member of the Provincial Health Services Authority and was funded through it, while remaining a Crown corporation with its own reporting.
records.establishedMeaning: established as a Crown corporation by Order in Council 1424 (November 1998); it took over the budget and staff of the ministry’s forensic psychiatric services on 1 April 1999
records.establishedLocator: Notes to the financial statements, years ended 31 March 2004 and 2003, note 1, Operations (PDF page 7, a scan)
records.endedMeaning: Its statements stop after 2003-04. It became a member of the Provincial Health Services Authority and in 2004 still described itself as a Crown corporation; the Forensic Psychiatry Act still provides for a commission, so no end is recorded.

attestations.scope: a Crown corporation and a member of PHSA, operating the Forensic Psychiatric Hospital and six community clinics
attestations.locator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1, Operations (PDF page 7)

records.name: British Columbia Health Research Foundation
records.description: A foundation incorporated under the British Columbia Health Research Foundation Act that funded health research. On its dissolution its rights, property and assets passed to the Michael Smith Foundation for Health Research, which also assumed its obligations.
records.endedMeaning: Dissolved when its Act was repealed under the Health Research Act (No. 2), 2002, brought in by an order approved on 11 July 2002; its last statements run to 17 October 2002. The day of dissolution is not stated, so neither date is taken as its end.

attestations.scope: final, unaudited statements prepared to this day
attestations.locator: Statement of financial position, period ended October 17, 2002

records.name: Private Post-Secondary Education Commission
records.description: Registered and regulated private post-secondary institutions in British Columbia until the Private Career Training Institutions Agency continued it in 2004.
records.establishedMeaning: the day the corporate registry records for the commission (BC Registries PA0000364)
records.establishedLocator: BC Registries (OrgBook BC), PA0000364, Private Post-Secondary Education Commission, registration 20 August 1990
records.endedMeaning: continued as the Private Career Training Institutions Agency, which was incorporated under the Private Career Training Institutions Act on 22 November 2004 and received all its assets and liabilities

records.name: Private Career Training Institutions Agency
records.description: A self-funding Crown agency that set basic education standards for registered private career training institutions, accredited institutions that met its quality standards, and protected their students, including through a student training completion fund. The ministry announced its dissolution in April 2014 and a public administrator replaced its board until it was dissolved.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated under the Private Career Training Institutions Act, as a continuation of the Private Post-Secondary Education Commission
records.endedMeaning: dissolved when the Private Training Act came into force; its assets, liabilities and functions passed to the Ministry of Advanced Education

records.name: Leading Edge Endowment Fund
records.description: A society set up by the Province to fund, on a matching basis, nineteen permanent British Columbia leadership chairs at post-secondary institutions and nine regional innovation chairs.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated under the Society Act (registered as the Advanced Research Endowment Society and renamed on 28 March 2002, the day it began operating)

names.name: Advanced Research Endowment Society
names.locator: BC Registries society S0044407: registration 20 March 2002; name change to Leading Edge Endowment Fund 28 March 2002

records.endedMeaning: Its operations ceased on 10 December 2012 and its wind-up was to be completed effective 31 December 2012; the registry lists the society as historical after a voluntary dissolution filing dated 19 November 2013. The legal end is not dated here.

operationalEnd.meaning: operations ceased; residual assets went to another entity in consultation with the Minister of Jobs, Tourism and Skills Training
operationalEnd.locator: Notes to the financial statements, notes 1 and 2

attestations.locator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1

records.name: Fraser Region Interim Aboriginal Authority
records.description: An interim authority, described in its statements as a Crown agency, that was to prepare the phased transfer of child and family services from the Ministry of Children and Family Development to a future Aboriginal authority in the Fraser region. It was funded by the Province through that ministry. On 31 March 2009 a regulation moved its assets, liabilities and records to the government and repealed the regulation that had set it up.
records.establishedMeaning: established under the Community Services Interim Authorities Act, as a continuation of the Fraser Region Aboriginal Planning Committee
records.endedMeaning: B.C. Reg. 58/2009, effective 31 March 2009, transferred its cash, receivables, capital assets, net assets, records and liabilities to the government and repealed B.C. Reg. 277/2007, the regulation that had established both interim authorities

attestations.scope: a Crown agency, preparing a phased transfer of resources and authority from the Ministry of Children and Family Development
attestations.locator: Notes to the financial statements for the seven and a half months ended 31 March 2008, note 1 (page 7, a scan)

records.name: Vancouver Island Aboriginal Transition Authority
records.description: An interim authority whose board of up to 12 members was chosen through a community process and appointed by the Province. It was to prepare for an Aboriginal child and family services authority on Vancouver Island and depended on funding from the Ministry of Children and Family Development. On 31 March 2009 a regulation moved its assets, liabilities and records to the government and repealed the regulation that had set it up.
records.establishedMeaning: created under the Community Services Interim Authorities Act, as a continuation of the Vancouver Island Aboriginal Transition Team
records.endedMeaning: B.C. Reg. 58/2009, effective 31 March 2009, transferred its cash, receivables, capital assets, net assets, records and liabilities to the government and repealed B.C. Reg. 277/2007, the regulation that had established both interim authorities

attestations.scope: operating, dependent on funding from the Ministry of Children and Family Development
attestations.locator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1, Purpose of the Transition Authority

records.name: B.C. Community Financial Services Corporation
records.description: A provincially owned savings institution, operating as Four Corners Community Savings, set up to bring banking and related services to residents of Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside. Only the Minister of Finance and Corporate Relations could hold its shares. After continuing losses the Province said on 4 December 2003 that it would fund it no further, and its board voted to suspend operations.
records.establishedMeaning: established under the Community Financial Services Act, SBC 1994
records.endedMeaning: the Community Financial Services Act was repealed effective this day and the corporation was dissolved; its branch had closed on 10 March 2004

operationalEnd.meaning: its branch closed to the public
operationalEnd.locator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1

records.name: Fisheries Renewal BC
records.description: A Crown corporation created to undertake strategic initiatives to renew the fisheries and enhance fish, fisheries and fish habitat in British Columbia, a counterpart to Forest Renewal BC.
records.establishedMeaning: the Fisheries Renewal Act, which established it, received assent
records.endedMeaning: the Fisheries Renewal Act was repealed effective 1 July 2002 (2002-7-6, B.C. Reg. 140/2002), dissolving the corporation; its last annual report says it closed on 31 March 2002

records.name: Rapid Transit Project 2000 Ltd.
records.description: The provincially owned company that designed and built the SkyTrain Millennium Line. TransLink began operating the line on 31 August 2002; the company filed statements with the Public Accounts until 2015-16.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated as 560255 B.C. Ltd.; renamed Rapid Transit Project 2000 Ltd. on 16 July 1998

names.name: 560255 B.C. Ltd.
names.locator: BC Registries company BC0560255: incorporation 25 February 1998; name change 16 July 1998

records.endedMeaning: dissolved (the registry records a voluntary dissolution)

records.name: Vancouver Convention Centre Expansion Project Ltd.
records.description: A company whose directors were all appointed by the Province, with the sole purpose of designing, building and commissioning the expansion of the convention centre in downtown Vancouver.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated under the Company Act
records.endedMeaning: amalgamated with the former B.C. Pavilion Corporation to form the present PavCo

records.name: Discovery Enterprises Inc.
records.description: A venture-investment company formed to administer the portfolio of the Discovery Enterprise Program, which the Province contributed through Discovery Foundation. The Province bought its shares from Discovery Foundation on 1 April 1994, after which it only managed and liquidated its existing investments in technology companies.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated under the Company Act as a wholly owned subsidiary of Discovery Foundation; it began operating on 1 April 1986
records.establishedLocator: BC Registries (OrgBook BC), company BC0306599, incorporation 24 March 1986
records.endedMeaning: wound up with its shareholder’s consent; its remaining assets and liabilities went to the shareholder, the Province

records.name: BCIF Management Ltd.
records.description: A company wholly owned by the Province that managed the British Columbia Investment Fund Ltd., set up to hold capital invested by immigrants; its statements consolidate the fund. The Public Accounts listed it with the self-supported Crown corporations.
records.establishedMeaning: incorporated, as BCGF Management Ltd.; renamed on 25 October 1995

names.name: BCGF Management Ltd.
names.locator: BC Registries company BC0486749: incorporation 23 December 1994; name change 25 October 1995

records.endedMeaning: dissolved by the registrar (the Registrar of Companies had given notice of dissolution on 2 May 2011); it ceased active business on 31 October 2006

operationalEnd.locator: Notes to the financial statements, note 1
